query: W melts near 3422 °C, whereas Cu boils near 2562 °C, so conventional induction or arc-plasma casting cannot readily yield a uniform W–Cu material. Phase separation and void formation can impair thermal transport. Filling a W skeleton with molten Cu or Cu powder can leave defects; spark-plasma sintering and mechanical alloying can produce finer, more uniform structures but can also leave voids; vapor-coated W powders have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents; and metal 3D printing has also been explored. Starting from W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix for heat transfer under irradiation in fusion-reactor joints, what single intervention could overcome these limitations while preserving mechanical durability? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts an outcome relative to a named existing fabrication baseline, defines the processing and service boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment and observations that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a liquid‐metal dealloying step on Ti‐alloyed tungsten (W) precursors, where sacrificial Ti-rich interdendritic channels are selectively leached in molten copper (Cu), will yield a W–Cu composite with a more uniform, void‐free, and aligned microstructure that enhances thermal transport and maintains mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation compared to vapor-coated sintered composites.
generation.material_initial_state: W particles or connected W regions combined with Ti-rich interdendritic phases within a Cu matrix precursor.
generation.intervention: A processing route that uses liquid‐metal dealloying in molten Cu to selectively remove the Ti-rich channels from a Ti-doped W structure.
generation.conditions: Processing in molten Cu at temperatures sufficiently high to promote dealloying but kept below the boiling point of Cu, under an inert atmosphere and with controlled dwell times to ensure selective Ti removal.
generation.structural_mediator: A restructured, aligned W framework uniformly infiltrated by Cu, exhibiting significantly reduced void fractions and improved interfacial bonding.
generation.mechanism: During exposure to molten Cu, the sacrificial Ti-rich interdendritic channels are preferentially leached out, leading to a reorganization of the W-Cu interface that minimizes phase separation and void formation, thereby providing enhanced thermal pathways and mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The liquid‐metal dealloyed composite will display superior thermal conductivity and improved mechanical durability under irradiation compared to baseline vapor-coated, sintered W powders, due to increased interfacial contact and fewer voids.
generation.baseline: Vapor-coated W powders that have been sintered to achieve near-perfect contact between the constituents.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies for processing temperatures below the boiling point of Cu and service conditions relevant to fusion-reactor joints under irradiation.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal processing parameters (e.g., dwell time, degree of Ti doping) and the long-term irradiation stability of the dealloyed structure remain to be determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of W–Cu composites: one using the established vapor-coated sintering method and the other using the proposed liquid-metal dealloying process on Ti-doped precursors. Characterize microstructures via SEM/TEM, measure void fractions, and perform thermal conductivity and mechanical tests (including under simulated irradiation conditions).
measurements: Microstructural analysis (SEM/TEM) to quantify void content and interfacial quality
Mechanical tests (tensile/fatigue) before and after simulated irradiation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dealloyed samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in thermal transport, reduced void formation, and enhanced mechanical durability under irradiation relative to the vapor-coated sintered samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
